campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business licenses and tobacco retailer permits for two local smoke shops. The Council also considered a resolution to apply for a regional transportation grant and a resolution approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance superseding prior rules implementing state Senate legislation
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for a cigar shop
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization to apply for a One Bay Area Grant for public works funding
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the city's intent to identify properties designated for a special assessment or district program. The Council also considered setting a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where residents could raise protests before the city finalizes its decision.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Scheduling of June 17, 2026 public hearing
Process for residents to file protests
Steps toward final approval of the property designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: At this Los Gatos Town Council meeting, members considered routine business including approval of prior meeting minutes and several contract amendments for ongoing town services. Items included extending agreements for tree care, legal services, and other town contracts, as well as authorizing the annual purchase of library books and materials, and reviewing the town's monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of June 16 and June 23, 2026 Council meeting minutes
Fourth amendment to the tree care services agreement with Brightview
Fifth amendment to the town's legal services contract
Annual authorization to purchase library books and materials from Ingram
Review of the monthly financial and investment report

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 12, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to finalize the City Council's agenda for August 18, 2026 and review the draft agenda for August 25, 2026, including deciding whether any items needed to be added or scheduled for a specific time. The committee also looked at when a study session should be released and reviewed the City Manager's monthly report of activities.
keyTopics: Finalizing the August 18, 2026 City Council agenda
Reviewing the draft August 25, 2026 agenda and adding new items
Assigning 'time certain' slots to specific agenda items
Checking whether any agenda items or documents needed notice waivers
Setting the release date for an upcoming study session and reviewing the City Manager's monthly activity report

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss city finances and infrastructure, including next year's budget limits, water supply planning, and capital projects like the Public Safety Building and Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving. Council also considered a closed-session item on potential litigation and issued several proclamations, including one honoring outgoing City Attorney Jennifer Logue's appointment to the judiciary.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation involving significant legal exposure (two potential cases)
Proclamations for National Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judicial appointment
Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget items, including the annual appropriations limit and updates to the city's financial policy
5-year update to the Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan
Capital projects including the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay Salt Pond Restoration

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: On July 28, 2026, the Sunnyvale City Council first met in a closed session to discuss confidential matters not open to the public. Afterward, in a special study session, the Council considered an update on the city's artificial turf policy, looking at how synthetic turf is used and regulated on public and private property.
keyTopics: Closed session (confidential Council discussion)
Artificial turf policy study update
Review of rules governing synthetic turf installation

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event and a Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program aimed at young drivers. Commissioners also heard about a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and approved minutes from their June meeting.
keyTopics: Planning for an upcoming Bike Fest event
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program for young drivers
Presentation on youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Public comment period for non-agenda items

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Station Area Task Force — July 16, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Station Area Task Force met on July 16, 2026, with the published agenda mainly covering standard legal disclosures about how residents could challenge certain city decisions. The available materials did not detail specific station area planning items discussed at this meeting.
keyTopics: Legal disclosure on filing deadlines for challenging city quasi-adjudicative decisions
Explanation of the 90-day limit under Code of Civil Procedure Section 1094.6
Standard procedural notices included with the meeting agenda

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot, which would replace the city's current business tax system with a tiered gross receipts tax. The proposal aims to base taxes more fairly on a business's actual economic activity while protecting small businesses, most of which would see minimal impact.
keyTopics: Ballot measure to modernize the city's business tax structure
Shift to a tiered gross receipts tax system
Protections for small businesses, which make up about 85% of Milpitas businesses
Comparing Milpitas's tax revenue and competitiveness to other cities
Simplifying tax administration and preparing for a changing economy, including tech and gig work

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — June 29, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council held a public hearing on a proposed development at 2468 South Court, considering a request to tear down an existing single-story house and detached garage and replace them with a new two-story, single-family home that includes a basement. An attached junior accessory dwelling unit was also shown as part of the plans, though it doesn't require the same level of city approval.
keyTopics: Proposed demolition of existing house and garage at 2468 South Court
Construction of new 2,481-square-foot two-story single-family home with 1,512-square-foot basement
Attached junior accessory dwelling unit (JADU) included for reference
Director's Review of Individual Review Application in R-1 single-family zoning district
Project deemed exempt from full environmental review under state CEQA rules
